326456.title: Extremality of the small-rainbow colouring for infinite graphs
326456.statement:
Let $\Delta:\mathbb{N}^{(2)}\twoheadrightarrow[k]$ be a surjective $k$-colouring of the edges of the complete graph on $\mathbb{N}$. For an infinite set $X\subset\mathbb{N}$, let $\gamma(X)=|\Delta[X^{(2)}]|$, and define

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}=\{\gamma(X):X\subset\mathbb{N}\text{ is infinite}\}.
$$

**Small-rainbow extremality conjecture.** If $n$ is a natural number and $k>\binom{n}{2}+1$, then

$$
\mathcal{F}_{\Delta}\cap\left(\binom{n}{2}+1,\binom{n+1}{2}+1\right]\ne\emptyset.
$$

The conjecture says that the small-rainbow colouring, which assigns distinct colours to the edges of an initial finite clique and one remaining colour to all other edges, is extremal for graphs. It predicts that every colouring with sufficiently many colours has an infinite subgraph whose number of colours lies in the indicated interval; the supplied text gives no resolution status.
326456.disposition: PARKED: finite-color surjective infinite Ramsey spectrum. Need a general forced color-count jump bound between consecutive triangular thresholds, not just small-rainbow examples; primary proof body unread.

326500.title: Main conjecture on Schur-positivity for complementary partition products
326500.statement:
Let $
u
oindent\text{ be a partition of }n$ and $\bmu$ a partition of $n+1$ such that $
u
oindent\text{ is contained in }\bmu$. Suppose complements are taken in the square $(m^m)$ with $m\geq \bmu_1+\ell(\bmu)$. The partition $\bmu$ **covers** $
u$ when $\bmu$ is obtained from $
u$ by adding one box.

**Main conjecture.** The partition $\bmu$ covers $
u$ if and only if (C1) $
u$ or $
u'$ has the form $\beta+(s^s)+\alpha$, where $\beta$ and $[?]$ are partitions, if $\beta_1=i$ then $\beta$ contains $(i^{s+1},i,i-1,i-2,\ldots,1)$, and $s\neq0$ if and only if $[?]$ is nonempty; and (C2) whenever $
u$ (respectively $
u'$) has this form, $\bmu$ (respectively $\bmu'$) is $\beta+(s^s,1)+\alpha$.

This is the paper's central proposed characterization of the cases in which the associated complementary Schur-function difference is Schur-positive. The supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.

326803.title: Gain-tightness characterization for symmetric sphere frameworks with horizontal or improper rotational symmetry
326803.statement: Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the sphere. For a $S$-symmetric framework, let $S$ be either the group $\mathcal{C}_{mh}$ with $m$ even or the group $\mathcal{S}_{2m}$ with $m$ odd. Let $(G,p)$ be an $S$-generic realisation on $\mathcal{S}$, and let $(G_0,\psi)$ be its quotient $S$-gain graph. A gain graph is **$(2,3,1)^i$-gain-tight** when it is $(2,3,1)^i$-gain-sparse and has $|F|=2|V(F)|-1$ for its full edge set, where the sparsity bounds are $|F|\leq 2|V(F)|-3$ when a nonempty edge set $F$ has vertex-generated subgroup $\mathcal{C}_1$ or $\mathcal{C}_i$, and $|F|\leq 2|V(F)|-1$ otherwise. **The sphere gain-tightness conjecture.** The framework $(G,p)$ is $S$-isostatic if and only if $(G_0,\psi)$ is $(2,3,1)^i$-gain-tight. This would complete the sphere characterizations for the remaining groups $\mathcal{C}_{mh}$ with even $m$ and $\mathcal{S}_{2m}$ with odd $m$; the source presents these cases as conjectural, while the analogous cases listed in the surrounding summary are established by the cited theorems.
326803.disposition: PARKED: gain-sparsity necessity does not prove symmetric generic rigidity sufficiency. Need orbit-rigidity rank for both complete symmetry families with all subgroup cases; primary body unread.

326918.title: Kadell's $q$-analogue of his constant-term hypothesis
326918.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $M\subset\{1,2,\dots,n\}$, and for each $s\in M$ choose an index $r_s$ such that $r_s\notin M$. Let $\boldsymbol{a}=(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ be nonnegative integers, and define $|\boldsymbol{a}|=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i$. For $1\leq i<j\leq n$, set

$$
a_i^*=a_i^*(j)=a_i+\chi(j\in M, i=r_j),\qquad a_j^*=a_j^*(i)=a_j+\chi(i\in M, j=r_i).
$$

With $(t)_k=(1-t)(1-tq)\dots(1-tq^{k-1})$, **Kadell's $q$-analogue of his constant-term hypothesis.** One has

$$
\operatorname{CT}\left[\prod_{1\leq i<j\leq n}\left(\frac{x_i}{x_j}\right)_{a_i^*}\left(\frac{qx_j}{x_i}\right)_{a_j^*}\right]=\frac{1-q^{1+|\boldsymbol{a}|}}{1-q^{1+\sum_{v\notin M}a_v}}\genfrac{[}{]}{0pt}{}{|\boldsymbol{a}|}{\boldsymbol{a}}.
$$

Kadell's earlier, more general non-$q$ hypothesis had recently been established by Zhou, but the source gives no resolution evidence for this $q$-analogue. Its significance is that it refines Dyson-type constant-term identities by prescribing contributions associated with the subset $M$.

360831.title: The $L^2$-Hall characterization for graphs of free groups with cyclic edge groups
360831.statement:
Let $X$ be a finite graph of groups with free vertex groups and cyclic edge groups, and let $G=\pi_1(X)$. Let $\Phi_X$ denote the associated graph used to identify the generalized Baumslag--Solitar components. A component is **solvable** when its associated generalized Baumslag--Solitar group is solvable.

**$L^2$-Hall characterization conjecture.** The following conditions should be equivalent:

1. $G$ has the $L^2$-Hall property.
2. Every component of $\Phi_X$ is solvable.
3. The generalized Baumslag--Solitar groups associated to the components of $\Phi_X$ all have the $L^2$-Hall property.

The paper motivates this conjecture by analogy with known criteria for subgroup separability and residual finiteness. The theorem immediately preceding it proves the $L^2$-Hall property under the stronger balanced-and-solvable, equivalently relatively hyperbolic, hypothesis; the equivalence proposed here remains open in the supplied text.

369893.title: Interlacing conjecture for Chow polynomials of simplicial posets
369893.statement:
Let $P$ be a simplicial poset, with associated polynomials $\operatorname{H}_{\widehat{P}}(x)$, $\operatorname{H}_{{\widehat{P}}^\ast}(x)$, and augmented polynomial $\operatorname{H}^{\operatorname{aug}}_{\widehat{P}}(x)$. **Interlacing conjecture.** The polynomials

$$
\operatorname{H}_{\widehat{P}}(x),\quad \operatorname{H}_{{\widehat{P}}^\ast}(x),\quad \operatorname{H}^{\operatorname{aug}}_{\widehat{P}}(x)
$$

are real-rooted. Moreover, the roots of both $\operatorname{H}_{\widehat{P}}(x)$ and $\operatorname{H}_{{\widehat{P}}^\ast}(x)$ interlace the roots of

$$
\operatorname{H}^{\operatorname{aug}}_{\widehat{P}}(x)=\operatorname{H}^{\operatorname{aug}}_{{\widehat{P}}^\ast}(x).
$$

The claim concerns real-rootedness and interlacing for Chow polynomials associated with simplicial posets; the supplied text gives no resolution beyond noting that related interlacing conjectures had appeared previously.

323333.title: Hiß–Lübeck–Malle conjecture on the shape and embedding of Brauer trees
323333.statement: Let $\Gamma$ be the Brauer tree of the principal $\Phi_h$-block. The characters $\chi_{m_\zeta}$ arise from the Frobenius eigenspaces in the rational $\ell$-adic cohomology, and the exceptional vertex is the vertex corresponding to the non-unipotent characters in the block. **Hiß–Lübeck–Malle conjecture.** (i) The vertices labelled by $\chi_{m_\zeta}$ are the only nodes connected to the exceptional node in $\Gamma$. (ii) The vertices labelled by $\chi_{m_\zeta}$ are ordered around the exceptional vertex according to increasing values of $m_\zeta$. This gives a precise prediction for the Brauer tree's shape and planar embedding from cohomological Frobenius data. The source presents this as the Hiß–Lübeck–Malle conjecture and the parser supplies no resolution status; the paper's abstract nevertheless states that the authors prove the conjecture in the cases considered.

323877.title: Walk enumeration conjecture for square non-zero recurrent configurations
323877.statement:
Let $D_{n,n}$ be the relevant complete bipartite graph with one sink, let $\mathsf{Rec}^{\star}(D_{n,n})$ denote its recurrent configurations, and write $u_1,\ldots,u_{m+n-1}$ for the heights at the non-sink vertices. Define

$$
a_n=\left\{u\in\mathsf{Rec}^{\star}(D_{n,n}):u_1,\ldots,u_{m+n-1}>0\right\}.
$$

**Square non-zero configuration conjecture.** The cardinality satisfies

$$
a_n=\frac{1}{n-1}\binom{2n-2}{n}\binom{2n}{n-2},
$$

and this is also the number of walks from $(0,0)$ to $(0,1)$ that remain in the upper half-plane $y\geq0$ and use $2n-3$ unit steps from $\{\mathsf{n},\mathsf{s},\mathsf{e},\mathsf{w}\}$.

The conjecture proposes a closed enumeration of square non-zero recurrent configurations and identifies the same numbers with constrained planar walks. The paper gives no proof or resolution beyond stating the conjecture.

324112.title: The three conjectural sporadics in the entropic order on a parabolic quotient of $S_6$
324112.statement:
In the above notation, let the displayed arrays denote the corresponding elements of the parabolic quotient, and let $\rhd$ denote the entropic partial order.

**Three sporadic entropic-order conjectures.** The following three relations hold:

$$
\begin{array}{rcl}
\mathbf{37}\rhd\mathbf{11}:\quad \left(\begin{array}{ccc}a & c & f\\b & d & e\end{array}\right)&\rhd&\left(\begin{array}{ccc}a & b & d\\f & c & e\end{array}\right),\\
\mathbf{43}\rhd\mathbf{11}:\quad \left(\begin{array}{ccc}a & d & e\\b & c & f\end{array}\right)&\rhd&\left(\begin{array}{ccc}a & b & d\\f & c & e\end{array}\right),\\
\mathbf{49}\rhd\mathbf{11}:\quad \left(\begin{array}{ccc}a & d & f\\b & c & e\end{array}\right)&\rhd&\left(\begin{array}{ccc}a & b & d\\f & c & e\end{array}\right).
\end{array}
$$

These are the remaining sporadic relations identified in the paper; the preceding discussion explains that the author was unable to prove them and that their structure does not yield to the techniques used for the other relations.

324271.title: The degree-ordering conjecture for subtree-maximizing trees
324271.statement:
Let $H$) be a tree, and consider any path between leaf vertices. For a path of odd length $2n-1$, suppose that the numbers of subtrees rooted at the successive branches satisfy

$$
C^H_1 \geq D^H_1 \geq C^H_2 \geq \ldots \geq C^H_n \geq D^H_n.
$$

For a path of even length $2n$, suppose that

$$
C^H_1 \geq D^H_1 \geq C^H_2 \geq \ldots \geq D^H_n \geq C^H_{n+1}.
$$

**Degree-ordering conjecture.** The degrees along the odd-length path must satisfy

$$
d(x_1) \geq d(y_1) \geq d(x_2) \geq \ldots \geq d(x_n) \geq d(y_n),
$$

and those along the even-length path must satisfy

$$
d(x_1) \geq d(y_1) \geq d(x_2) \geq \ldots \geq d(y_n) \geq d(x_{n+1}).
$$

The claim asks whether the degree-switches used in the paper are unnecessary: the ordering obtained after the first two phases would already force the degree ordering targeted in Phase III. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

358443.title: Duncan–Steingrímsson's Bell-number conjecture for modified ascent sequences
358443.statement:
A **modified ascent sequence** is a combinatorial sequence of integers equipped with the ascent-pattern avoidance notion used here; a pattern is avoided when it does not occur as a pattern in the sequence. The six patterns under consideration are

$$
212,\;1212,\;2132,\;2213,\;2231,\;2321.
$$

**Duncan–Steingrímsson's conjecture.** On modified ascent sequences, these six patterns are all Wilf-equivalent, and the enumeration of modified ascent sequences avoiding any one of them is given by the Bell numbers. Moreover, the distribution of the number of ascents is the reverse of the distribution of blocks on set partitions.

The conjecture concerns pattern avoidance in Fishburn-type combinatorial structures and predicts both a common Bell-number enumeration and a refined correspondence with set partitions. The paper describes the corresponding Fishburn permutations by pattern avoidance and presents the work as mostly devoted to proving this conjecture; the supplied text does not state whether every part has been resolved.

340020.title: Andrews–Gordon-type q-series identities for the Kanade–Russell conjectures
340020.statement:
Let $(a;q)_\infty=\prod_{j\geq 0}(1-aq^j)$ and $(a;q)_n=\prod_{j=0}^{n-1}(1-aq^j)$ denote the $q$-Pochhammer symbols. Let $q$ be a formal variable, and let all summation indices in the displayed identities range over non-negative integers.

**Kanade–Russell q-series conjectures.** The following identities are conjectured:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{(q,q^3,q^6,q^8;q^9)_\infty}&=\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{3n_2^2+n_1^2+3n_1n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}},\\
\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^6,q^7;q^9)_\infty}&=\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{3n_2^2+3n_2+n_1^2+n_1+3n_1n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}},\\
\frac{1}{(q^3,q^4,q^5,q^6;q^9)_\infty}&=\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{3n_2^2+3n_2+n_1^2+2n_1+3n_1n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}},\\
\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^5,q^8;q^9)_\infty}&=\sum_{n_1,n_2\geq0}\frac{q^{3n_2^2+2n_2+n_1^2+n_1+3n_1n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^3;q^3)_{n_2}}.
\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{(q,q^3,q^4,q^6,q^7,q^{10},q^{11};q^{12})_\infty}&=\sum_{n_1,n_2,n_3\geq0}\frac{q^{(9n_3^2+5n_3)/2+2n_2^2+n_2+n_1^2+6n_3n_2+3n_3n_1+2n_2n_1}(-q;q^2)_{n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^2;q^2)_{n_2}(q^3;q^3)_{n_3}}\\
&=\sum_{n_1,m_2,n_3,m_4\geq0}\frac{q^{8m_4^2+2m_4+(9n_3^2+5n_3)/2+(5m_2^2+m_2)/2+n_1^2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q;q)_{m_2}(q^3;q^3)_{n_3}(q^4;q^4)_{m_4}}q^{12m_4n_3+8m_4m_2+4m_4n_1+6n_3m_2+3n_3n_1+2m_2n_1},\\
\frac{1}{(q^2,q^3,q^5,q^6,q^7,q^8,q^{11};q^{12})_\infty}&=\sum_{n_1,n_2,n_3\geq0}\frac{q^{(9n_3^2+7n_3)/2+2n_2^2+3n_2+n_1^2+n_1+6n_3n_2+3n_3n_1+2n_2n_1}(-q;q^2)_{n_2}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q^2;q^2)_{n_2}(q^3;q^3)_{n_3}}\\
&=\sum_{n_1,m_2,n_3,m_4\geq0}\frac{q^{8m_4^2+6m_4+(9n_3^2+7n_3)/2+(5m_2^2+5m_2)/2+n_1^2+n_1}}{(q;q)_{n_1}(q;q)_{m_2}(q^3;q^3)_{n_3}(q^4;q^4)_{m_4}}q^{12m_4n_3+8m_4m_2+4m_4n_1+6n_3m_2+3n_3n_1+2m_2n_1}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These identities arise by setting the part-counting variable to $1$ in generating functions for partition counters associated with the Kanade–Russell conjectures. The supplied text presents them as conjectured identities in conjunction with Kanade and Russell's work, but gives no resolution status for these $q$-series formulations.

332117.title: Generator matrix conjecture for quasi-cyclic product codes in Pre-RGB/POT form
332117.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an $[n_A=\ell_A m_A,k_A,d_A]_q$ $\ell_A$-quasi-cyclic code with generator matrix $G_A(X)\in\mathbb{F}_q[X]^{\ell_A\times\ell_A}$, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be an $[n_B=\ell_B m_B,k_B,d_B]_q$ $\ell_B$-quasi-cyclic code with generator matrix $G_B(X)\in\mathbb{F}_q[X]^{\ell_B\times\ell_B}$. Set $m=m_A m_B$ and $\ell=\ell_A\ell_B$. For $g\in\{0,\ldots,\ell_B-1\}$ and $h\in\{0,\ldots,\ell_A-1\}$, define

$$
g_{g+h\ell_B,g+h\ell_B}(X)=\gcd\left(X^m-1,\,G_{A,h,h}(X^{b n_B})G_{B,g,g}(X^{a n_A})\right).
$$

Choose $u_{g,h}(X),v_{g,h}(X)\in\mathbb{F}_q[X]$ satisfying

$$
g_{g+h\ell_B,g+h\ell_B}(X)=u_{g,h}(X)(X^m-1)+v_{g,h}(X)G_{A,h,h}(X^{b n_B})G_{B,g,g}(X^{a n_A}).
$$

**Generator matrix conjecture.** A generator matrix in $\mathbb{F}_q[X]^{\ell\times\ell}$, in Pre-RGB/POT form, for the $[n=\ell m,k_Ak_B,d_Ad_B]_q$ $\ell$-quasi-cyclic product code $\mathcal{A}\otimes\mathcal{B}$ is given by the displayed upper-triangular matrix with diagonal entries above, multiplied by

$$
\operatorname{diag}\left(1,X^{\nu(1,0)},\ldots,X^{\nu(\ell_B-1,0)},\ldots,X^{\nu(\ell_B-1,\ell_A-1)}\right),
$$

where its off-diagonal entries are

$$
\overline{g}_{g+h\ell_B,g'+h'\ell_B}(X)=v_{g,h}(X)G_{A,h,h'}(X^{b n_B})G_{B,g,g'}(X^{a n_A})\pmod{X^m-1}
$$

for $g\in\{0,\ldots,\ell_B-1\}$, $h\in\{0,\ldots,\ell_A-1\}$, $g'\in\{g+1,\ldots,\ell_B-1\}$, and $h'\in\{h+1,\ldots,\ell_A-1\}$. The parameters $a,b$ and the shift function $\nu$ are those used in the construction of the product code and its coordinate ordering.

346916.title: The finitely generated groups twin-width conjecture
346916.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a countable group generated by a finite set $S$, and let $\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$ be its Cayley graph with vertex set $\Gamma$ and edges $\{x,x\cdot s\}$ for $x\in\Gamma$ and $s\in S$. Let $F(\Gamma,S)$ be the class of all finite induced subgraphs of $\operatorname{Cay}(\Gamma,S)$.

**Finitely generated groups conjecture.** For every group $\Gamma$ generated by a finite set $S$, the class $F(\Gamma,S)$ has bounded twin-width.

The question is motivated by the examples of free groups and the integer grid, whose associated classes have bounded twin-width. The supplied text presents this as the main question of the section and gives no resolution.

325371.title: The chromatic bound conjecture for the first Steklov eigenvalue
325371.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a compact surface with boundary. Write $m_1(\Sigma)$ for the maximal multiplicity of the first Steklov eigenvalue $\sigma_1(\Sigma,g,\rho,\gamma)$ as the metric $g$ and the positive densities $\rho$ and $\gamma$ vary. Let $\mathrm{Chr}_0(\Sigma)$ be the supremum of the chromatic numbers of finite graphs admitting a proper embedding in $\Sigma$, where proper means that every vertex is mapped to $\partial\Sigma$. **Chromatic bound conjecture.** For every compact surface $\Sigma$ with boundary, 

$$
m_1(\Sigma)=\mathrm{Chr}_0(\Sigma)-1.
$$

This conjecture relates the multiplicity of the first Steklov eigenvalue to the relative chromatic number of the surface. The supplied text gives no evidence of a resolution.

339488.title: The kaon–glide positivity conjecture
339488.statement:
A weak composition is a finite sequence of nonnegative integers. For weak compositions $a$ and $b$, let $\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_a$ denote the kaon associated with $a$, and let $\overline{\mathfrak{F}}_b$ denote the glide polynomial associated with $b$. **Kaon–glide positivity conjecture.** For any weak compositions $a$ and $b$, the product

$$
\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_a\cdot\overline{\mathfrak{F}}_b
$$

expands as a positive sum of kaons. This is a proposed positive structure theorem for the $K$-theoretic kaon basis, whose individual structure coefficients need not otherwise be positive.

328902.title: Benjamini–Georgakopoulos conjecture on local indistinguishability of Cayley graphs
328902.statement:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finitely presented group, and let $F$ be a connected, locally finite Cayley graph of $\Gamma$. A graph is **$r$-locally $F$** if every radius-$r$ ball in it is isomorphic to a radius-$r$ ball in $F$.

**Benjamini–Georgakopoulos conjecture.** There exists $r\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, whenever a graph $G$ is $r$-locally $F$, $F$ covers $G$.

This conjecture proposes a general structure theorem for graphs locally indistinguishable from a Cayley graph. It was disproved by de la Salle and Tessera; the additional assumption discussed immediately before the conjecture is necessary for the positive results that followed.

381294.title: Harary–Schwenk–Scott conjecture for locally finite trees
381294.statement: Let $G$ be a locally finite tree. A graph $G$ is **reconstructible** if every graph hypomorphic to $G$ is isomorphic to $G$, where hypomorphism means that there is a bijection between the vertex sets whose corresponding vertex-deleted induced subgraphs are isomorphic. **Harary–Schwenk–Scott conjecture.** Every locally finite tree is reconstructible. The conjecture arose after non-reconstructible infinite graphs and locally finite forests were found, and it was proposed as the corresponding positive statement for locally finite trees. The paper constructs a counterexample, so the conjecture is refuted.

351826.title: The logarithmic treewidth conjecture excluding cliques, bicliques and induced walls
351826.statement:
Let $t\geq 0$, let $K_t$ be the complete graph on $t$ vertices, and let $K_{t,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with $t$ vertices in each part. Let $W_{t\times t}$ be the $t\times t$ wall, and let a subdivision and a line graph have their usual meanings. Write $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ for the treewidth of $G$ and $V(G)$ for its vertex set.

**Induced-wall exclusion conjecture.** For all $t\geq 0$, there exists a constant $c=c(t)$ such that every graph $G$ with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_t$, $K_{t,t}$, a subdivision of $W_{t\times t}$, or the line graph of a subdivision of $W_{t\times t}$ satisfies

$$
\operatorname{tw}(G)\leq c\log(|V(G)|).
$$

The source presents this as a possible variant of a conjecture from the cited earlier work and gives no resolution, so it remains open.

353903.title: Local List Linear Hadwiger's Conjecture
353903.statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $v(G)$ denote its number of vertices, and let $B_c[v]$ be the subgraph induced by the vertices at distance at most $c$ from $v$. For a positive integer $c$, call $G$ **$c$-locally-$K_t$-minor-free** if $B_c[v]$ has no $K_t$ minor for every vertex $v\in V(G)$. A graph is $k$-list-colourable if it is colourable from every list assignment with lists of size at least $k$. **Local List Linear Hadwiger's Conjecture.** For every positive integer $t$, there exists a constant $c_1>0$ depending on $t$, and a constant $c_2>0$, such that every graph $G$ which is $\lceil c_1\log(v(G))\rceil$-locally-$K_t$-minor-free is $c_2t$-list-colourable. This is a local list-colouring strengthening of Linear Hadwiger's Conjecture and remains open; the source gives partial results for related local colouring statements.
